title: KISS TAVRN budgeted EDF redundant bearer
goal: Improve raw BLE advertising bearer resilience with bounded rolling airtime, priority-banded EDF expiry, selectively repeated atomic sweeps, and measured queue capacity while preserving current network ownership and protocol semantics.
scope: Use a true rolling 1000 ms budget with 40 total BU, 32 general BU, and 8 reply-critical reserve BU
Use mandatory expiry and priority-banded EDF for the routed fixed-array TX queue
Keep one-sweep and two-sweep operations atomic and reserve their full cost before TX
Use two sweeps for every wire RREQ, every wire RREP, DATA, and bootstrap HELLO; use one sweep for current remaining frame classes
Fix response release time from the first repeated request copy so duplicates cannot postpone or recreate a pending response
Drop and count expired anonymous work; emit an expiry scheduler event for custody DATA and controls already tracked by the existing token path
Remove generalized owner-domain/global-reset scaffolding introduced during this branch instead of expanding protocol ownership
Measure final memory, timing, queue behavior, delivery, retries, blackout, and duplicate reception for capacities 4, 8, 16, and 40 before selecting production capacity
nonGoals: Add standard Bluetooth Mesh, SoftDevice, GATT, connections, or Link Layer ARQ
Add token domains, ownership tracking, or delivery semantics to previously anonymous mentorship, RERR, FLOOD, maintenance, relay, HELLO, or TC traffic
Create a production caller for the currently unused originated-FLOOD API
Use dynamic allocation, a tree/heap queue, global EDF, or simultaneous multi-channel RX
Flash or roll out firmware without explicit approval
constraints: Keep network semantics out of the radio driver
Use fixed-size storage, bounded linear scans, no heap, and no recursion
One BU equals one ordered 37/38/39 sweep; a two-sweep operation reserves two BU atomically
Nothing bypasses the 40-BU total cap; general work cannot consume the 8-BU critical reserve
Critical reserve eligibility is limited to HACK, RREP, RREP_ACK, SYNC_OFFER, and SYNC_DATA; RREQ, DATA, and bootstrap HELLO remain general
Preserve existing priority bands: HACK above retry, control, DATA, and relay; apply EDF only within a priority band
Preserve existing token behavior; token NONE remains anonymous and existing low/high token ranges remain routed through current scheduler events
Preserve the 5000 ms absolute DATA transaction deadline and current retry ceiling

The first received request-copy timestamp is authoritative: HACK, RREP, and RREP_ACK release at that fixed timestamp +14+8 ms regardless of later decision latency; SYNC_OFFER releases at first bootstrap-HELLO timestamp +14 ms + the existing mentorship delay
No hardware flash, reset, clean, checkout, commit, or deletion without explicit approval

steps.title: Record available mixed-worktree evidence and its limit
steps.target: branch/base commit, D2 source hashes, F6 evidence, known pre-bearer custody/router behavior
steps.action: Preserve all pre-bearer custody/router changes without reset or flash. Record that no restorable pre-bearer patch was captured, so shared-file hunks require manual intent review rather than automated attribution.
steps.validation: The plan cites available evidence and never claims the base commit or D2 aggregate digest can reconstruct the pre-bearer worktree.

steps.title: Parameterize routed queue capacity
steps.target: profile CMake, generated config/manifest, queue layout
steps.action: Support routed capacities 4, 8, 16, and 40 while LEGACY and LINK remain fixed at 4.
steps.validation: Variants build and initial linker-map deltas are recorded without legacy/link growth.

steps.title: Add focused bearer contract tests
steps.target: queue, scheduler, radio shim, link, timers
steps.action: Cover EDF metadata/selection, rolling budget, repeated radio operations, timer formulas, and frame mapping with focused host tests.
steps.validation: Each completed mechanic has a focused green test mode.

phases.title: Core KISS queue, scheduler, and radio mechanics

steps.title: Implement expiry metadata and priority-banded EDF selection
steps.action: Store mandatory expiry and select released, non-expired work by priority, earliest expiry within that priority, then oldest ordinal. Expired retirement is a separate active slice.
steps.validation: Priority, EDF, ordinal, expiry exclusion, equality, and wrap tests pass.

steps.title: Implement rolling BU accounting and custody hold
steps.action: Reserve complete operation cost against 40 total, 32 general, and 8 critical-reserve BU in a true rolling 1000 ms window; remain in RX when denied.
steps.validation: Cost, wrap, equality, reserve, no-refund, and no-fallback tests pass.

steps.title: Implement atomic one/two-sweep radio operations
steps.target: raw RADIO driver and host shim
steps.action: Execute ordered 37/38/39 or 37/38/39 twice under one RX blackout and retain per-sweep completion evidence.
steps.validation: Order, requested/completed masks, partial results, and cleanup tests pass.

steps.title: Publish canonical operation and custody timing bounds
steps.action: Publish and validate the 8 ms one-sweep, 14 ms two-sweep, 18 ms cleanup, budgeted attempt, response-window, and absolute DATA deadline formulas.
steps.validation: Generated values, validation, manifests, and focused timer tests agree.

phases.title: Frame mapping, fixed responses, and KISS expiry closure

steps.title: Finalize sweep and reserve-class mapping
steps.action: Apply wire-type precedence: every RREQ/RREP is two sweeps regardless of producer; DATA and bootstrap HELLO are two; all others are one. Limit critical reserve to HACK, RREP, RREP_ACK, SYNC_OFFER, and SYNC_DATA; change no ownership semantics.
steps.validation: Link/incarnation tests cover sweep count and budget class for each exceptional class; profile gates pass.

steps.title: Fix first-copy response release
steps.target: tavrn_link_v2; aodv_core/tavrn_router existing RREQ/RREP dedupe; tavrn_mentorship existing bootstrap pending state
steps.action: Capture the first RX timestamp before candidate/action resolution and keep at most one pending response per existing request key. HACK, RREP, and RREP_ACK release at fixed first-RX +14+8 ms regardless of decision latency; SYNC_OFFER releases at first bootstrap-HELLO RX +14 ms + the existing mentorship delay. A later retry may respond after the first pending response transmitted or expired.
steps.validation: First/second copy, delayed decision/candidate timeout, first status, after-send retry, exact fixed +22 ms direct-reply release, mentorship delay, wrap, cancellation, and expiry tests pass.

steps.title: Remove over-scoped terminal ownership scaffolding
steps.target: ble_mesh_tx_queue; ble_mesh_scheduler; tavrn_link_v2; focused future-bearer tests
steps.action: Remove branch-added AODV/maintenance/repair/mentorship owner kinds, LOW/HIGH owner domains, synchronous global-owner reset, and compatibility callback. Preserve the existing queue token and scheduler-event routing used before this bearer work.
steps.validation: No branch-added protocol owner domain remains; anonymous token NONE and existing tracked/custody tokens retain completion, failure, eviction, and cancellation behavior.

steps.title: Retire expired entries through existing scheduler events
steps.target: queue collector; routed scheduler poll; tavrn_link_v2; tavrn_router; tavrn_full_maintenance_binding; tavrn_maintenance; tavrn_full_repair_binding; tavrn_repair; existing token counters
steps.action: At the start of routed poll, before selection and budget checks, purge bounded anonymous expiry and surface at most one token-bearing expiry as TX_EXPIRED. The event carries the queued token, requested channel mask, and requested sweep count; attempted sweep count, completed mask, and all per-sweep completed masks are zero. Add explicit TX_EXPIRED handling to each existing low/high/custody token consumer as an unsent deadline terminal, without TX_DONE side effects or normalization to radio TX_FAILED. Add no owner domain or cross-protocol reset.
steps.validation: Anonymous purge/count and capacity release; expiry-before-selection ordering; custody, metadata, targeted, verification, and repair existing-token expiry; equality/wrap; one-token event per poll; exact event masks/counts; and no-silent-discard tests pass.

steps.title: Reconcile normative docs with KISS scope
steps.target: profile, ACK, architecture, deviations, test matrix
steps.action: Remove generalized owner/global-reset claims and document only implemented bearer mechanics, token-preserving expiry events, fixed first-copy responses, budget/EDF rules, and benchmark requirements.
steps.validation: Docs, requirement IDs, generated formulas, and implementation agree without future-owner claims.

phases.title: Non-perturbing benchmark evidence and capacity decision

steps.title: Freeze the observer-v3 application contract
steps.target: benchmark firmware, analyzer, comparison output, six-role runner
steps.action: Use the approved KISS accepted-only observer-v3 contract: compact per-accepted and per-final identity/timestamp evidence, exact workload-split cumulative offered/accepted/rejected/not-ready counters, accepted PDR as authoritative, offered PDR labeled separately, and no claim of exact per-window rejection identities. Match by origin session plus compact identity and preserve source-offer to destination-delivery latency.
steps.validation: The wire grammar, accounting equations, validity domains, queue/drop semantics, record-order rules, and capture-boundary behavior are explicit and analyzer tests cover them.

steps.title: Make benchmark telemetry non-perturbing
steps.target: routed_benchmark state/queues, routed benchmark integration, observer-v3 analyzer/tests, resource gates
steps.action: Replace duplicated OFFER/APPLICATION logging with a compact accepted-event FIFO and workload-split counters. Add a compact final-event FIFO whose saturation drops and invalidates telemetry but never returns delivery BUSY. Use atomic event/checkpoint accounting, prioritize critical accept/final evidence over auxiliary control/GTT output, expose existing router reserve/commit BUSY counters, and keep non-benchmark MIND behavior unchanged. Add no speculative scheduler counters in this slice.
steps.validation: Focused C/Python tests pass; source/final queue equations are exact at complete checkpoints; terminal partial lines are safely right-censored; benchmark final telemetry fullness cannot backpressure router delivery; observer fixed state and total BSS do not exceed the prechange benchmark baseline without an explicit reviewed exception.

steps.title: Validate canonical FULL load and rerun AODV comparison
steps.target: host/resource checks and pinned six-board queue-40 two-sweep runs
steps.action: The 130-second smoke and recovered 1200-second FULL_TAVRN queue-40 runs are complete with valid application, transport, control, and clock evidence. Preserve the canonical FULL bundle, then rerun AODV after reboot and use compare_tavrn_benchmarks.py for the final side-by-side application and control-proxy comparison. Keep GTT formally INCOMPLETE for the single role-E cadence violation even though reporting recovered.
steps.validation: FULL evidence remains checksummed and reproducible with zero invalid telemetry intervals, zero critical observer/transport drops, and exact accepted/final accounting. The next AODV run must use the same observer-v3 contract and produce a finalized bundle before the comparison/capacity decision is closed.

steps.title: Run complete software and resource closure
steps.target: focused, protocol, application, profile, resource, and D2 gates
steps.action: Run narrow checks first, then the complete existing suite. Review each final hunk against the KISS scope and known pre-bearer behavior; use available D2 source hashes as evidence only where applicable and do not claim automated pre-bearer reconstruction.
steps.validation: All required checks are green; no unused owner/reset scaffolding remains; manual hunk review records any shared pre-bearer file that cannot be mechanically attributed.

steps.title: Roll out selected production build only after approval
steps.action: After benchmark selection and explicit approval, flash the selected capacity/policy and start any requested long stress run.
steps.validation: Budget caps, RX blackout, delivery, retries, expiry, queue behavior, and terminal faults meet the approved gates.
